defects.description: The comparison `if x < max_num` keeps the smallest value seen, so the function returns the minimum instead of the maximum; it should be `>`.
paraphrases: `<` should be `>`; find_max must track the largest value.
Using `<` makes the function compute the minimum.
find_max([2,4,9,...]) would return the smallest element, not 94.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `if x > max_num`. Real (returns the min), findable via the docstring, distinct.

defects.description: The running maximum is initialised to `0` instead of the first element, so for all-negative inputs the function wrongly returns 0.
paraphrases: `max_num = 0` should be `max_num = nums[0]`; 0 is not a valid starting maximum.
For a list of negatives, starting at 0 returns 0, which is not in the list.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `max_num = nums[0]`. Real (wrong for all-negative inputs), findable via the docstring, distinct.

defects.description: The empty-input guard tests `len(nums) == 1`, so an empty list is not caught (it raises IndexError elsewhere) while a valid single-element list is wrongly rejected.
paraphrases: `len(nums) == 1` should be `len(nums) == 0`; the guard is meant to catch empty input.
A one-element list is rejected while an empty list slips through.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `len(nums) == 0`. Real (wrong inputs guarded), findable via the docstring (find_max([5]) == 5), distinct.
